trajectory_summary: The call opens cold and never warms — the customer cooperates through a lengthy, frustrating bill-navigation struggle, then uses a disclosed family emergency to exit and asks to be removed from Ion's contact list. Energy leaked steadily from the moment the app struggle began, and the rep never recovered it with reassurance, a scope pivot, or a clean close.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear; observed outcome should be no_appointment or dq-by-withdrawal, not any form of booked/tentative. The customer explicitly declines to proceed ('That is not something that I'm interested in doing right now') and asks for contact removal — no appointment or callback time was set.

observed_outcome.quote: That is not something that I'm interested in doing right now.
observed_outcome.reasoning: No day or time was ever proposed or agreed to; the call ends with the customer requesting removal from Ion's contact list, which is the opposite of a booked or tentative appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: So average, maybe about a 100 or more. But, of course, you know, that varies depending on the time of year.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured a workable ballpark bill figure early but never used it as emotional leverage or a reason to act — instead of flipping to alignment-against-the-utility, the rep spent the next seven-plus minutes chasing a more precise kWh figure through a frustrating app struggle, which is exactly where the flip should have gone instead.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asked what interested the customer in solar (verify.interest_in_solar) — the call moved directly from intro into address/homeowner/utility/bill verify items without ever surfacing the customer's motivation, so there was no emotional anchor available to reinforce later.

we can put you on the schedule if we get the last three months.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: I have a a family emergency that came up, so this is kind of the lowest priority.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer handed the rep a direct, real reason for disengaging and the rep's only response was 'Okay' before continuing logistics — this is the single biggest relationship-repair opportunity missed on the call and it's a named schema pattern (coaching_philosophy.empathy_on_vulnerability_disclosure).

key_moments.quote: Are you So sorry. Are you logged in to the app right now?
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer had already given a workable ballpark ('60 to a 100... but summer months were even higher') from her own spreadsheet. Instead of using that number to anchor the conversation, the rep pushed her into the utility app, starting a seven-minute detour.

key_moments.quote: I'm not seeing a yearly kilowatt hours.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the point where bill_collection's own alternative-path guidance calls for a pivot to verbal read-back within about two minutes of friction. The rep is already past that window and continues coaching the customer through app navigation instead.

key_moments.quote: Well, the last three months, it will be a month and a half of service. So that makes no sense
key_moments.stewart_read: By this point the customer is pointing out the data itself is unreliable (she wasn't home for six months), yet the rep continues pursuing the same data-capture goal instead of stepping back and offering to defer bill collection to the specialist appointment.

key_moments.quote: I have a a family emergency that came up, so this is kind of the lowest priority.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a direct vulnerability disclosure — a family emergency, one of the schema's named trigger categories. The rep's entire response is a flat 'Okay,' with no acknowledgment of the situation before continuing the call mechanics.
